technical_facts: Quake 2 architecture uses a separate .dll file for game logic instead of the Quake 1 .qc language to improve efficiency (estimated 5-10% speed increase) and allow use of native code.
Quake 2 implements 'areaportals' to divide maps into areas, allowing the engine to cull rendering and sound for areas not reachable via open portals, regardless of the PVS (Potentially Visible Set).
The Quake 2 BSP format (version 38) supports up to 65,536 planes, nodes, leafs, and brush sides.
QuakeWorld networking uses delta compression to minimize bandwidth and supports up to 32 players.
The Quake 2 rendering architecture allows switching between software and OpenGL modes without restarting the game.
SGI Origin-2000 servers with MIPS R10000 processors were used for high-end compute tasks due to better scalability and cost-per-CPU compared to enterprise Intel systems.
The .md2 triangle model format uses a scaled byte representation for vertices to fit within frame mins/maxs.
UDP is preferred over TCP for real-time gaming to avoid the latency caused by TCP's error recovery mechanisms.
Quake 2 uses a dedicated network thread and checksums maps on the client side to prevent 'cheater maps'.
The 'Trinity' project research involves progressive mesh style LOD rendering and radiosity-based sound solutions.
personality_patterns: Extreme focus on technical excellence and writing 'the best software I can'.
Pragmatic approach to feature sets: willing to cut 'pet features' if they obstruct future architectural expansion.
Transparent and direct communication style, often using public .plan files to document decisions and frustrations.
High tolerance for sleep deprivation in pursuit of development goals.
Preference for small, high-efficiency teams over large groups to avoid communication overhead and entropy.
Passion for high-performance machinery, specifically Ferraris and drag racing.
Openly welcomes insightful technical criticism but dislikes implied ulterior motives or cynicism regarding his motivations.

gnosis_principles.description: The true cost of adding a feature is not just the initial coding time, but the long-term obstacle it creates for future expansion and the fragility it adds to the codebase.
There is a limit to programming team size beyond which adding more people increases development time due to communication overhead and the loss of global scope of knowledge.

A software project is never truly finished; waiting for every feature to be perfect prevents shipping. The value of releasing a functional product early often outweighs the benefit of a 'perfect' later release.
A single developer with a global understanding of the entire system (editor, utilities, game) is more efficient than multiple developers with specialized, local knowledge.

heritage_patterns: Use of BSP (Binary Space Partitioning) trees for both rendering and environment testing.
Client-side prediction to mask network latency in real-time multiplayer.
Modular game logic exported to external libraries (DLLs) to separate engine from game rules.
Development of custom internal tools (e.g., 3D model painting programs, map editors) when commercial options fail to meet specific technical needs.

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did Carmack decide to move from .qc to DLLs for Quake 2?
dpo_pairs.chosen: To improve efficiency by using native code, which provided a 5-10% speed increase, and to allow for more sophisticated game logic and easier debugging with real debuggers.
dpo_pairs.rejected: Because he wanted to make the game harder to mod for people who didn't know how to use a compiler.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is the purpose of 'areaportals' in Quake 2?
dpo_pairs.chosen: They allow the engine to cull rendering and sound for entire areas of a map if no open portals lead to them, providing a more effective culling mechanism than PVS alone, especially for doors.
dpo_pairs.rejected: They are used to create fancy teleportation effects between different levels of the game.

dpo_pairs.prompt: How does Carmack view the relationship between team size and productivity?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He believes there is a maximum optimal team size, beyond which adding more programmers actually slows down development due to communication overhead and the loss of a global architectural perspective.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He believes that more programmers always lead to a better product if they are managed correctly.
